newsitem.title: FINLAND: FINNISH BANKS CALM ON DEPOSIT GUARANTEE PROPOSAL.
newsitem.headline: FINNISH BANKS CALM ON DEPOSIT GUARANTEE PROPOSAL.

text.p: Finnish banks see only a mild impact from a proposed ceiling on state guarantees for bank deposits, an official at a bank lobby told a news conference on Tuesday.

"It may have some impact on clients' behaviour, at least during a transition period, but I don't see any major upheaval in the long term," Erkki Kontkanen, director of the Finnish Bankers' Association told a news conference.
He did not elaborate on to what extent funds currently in bank deposits might be flowing into other instruments, but said such shifts would be marginal.
A finance ministry working group on Tuesday submitted a proposal that state guarantees on deposits be limited to 150,000 markka from current guarantees for unlimited deposit amounts.

Kontkanen said the lowering of the guarantee ceiling would not have any impact on banks' earnings, and it would only have a marginal impact on deposits as the number of deposits exceeding 150,000 markka was small.

According to the working group's report, the proposed deposit guarantee would fully cover 96 percent of the number of deposits, and cover about 60 percent of the value of the public's deposits with banks.
"This type of limit has been in use for a long time in all European countries except Germany, and it has not caused any shake-up," Kontkanen said.
The working group also proposed that a new deposit guarantee fund would be established. All deposit banks should join the new fund.
Legislation on new deposit guarantees should take effect at the beginning of 1998, whereafter membership in the current guarantee funds of different bank groups would be voluntary, the report said.
